ext4_experiment.limits: Synthetic 19-page owner and 6-page root with a 6 MiB outcome payload. This is feasibility evidence only. It does not show maximum checkpoint or proof sizes, the production volume, host backing storage, or power-loss behaviour.

measurements.shape: Real protected root (CreateFreshProtectedRoot) and real SQLite owner. Every identifier is 256 bytes of '<' plus a short tag. '<' is valid under validID and encodes as \u003c, six bytes each, so the encoded identifier field is 1536 bytes. One transcript. Synthetic digests.
api_sequence_per_tool_call: ReserveEffect (consumes the captured call; returns the receipt)
measurements.owner_commits_note: Counted from workflow_recovery_state.sequence before and after each API call; each call moved the sequence by exactly one. Production call sites: ReserveEffect at cmd/tbound/governed_session_linux.go:584 and RecordTerminalEffectOutcome at cmd/tbound/governed_workflow_live_linux.go:751. Not re-run through cmd/tbound in this round.
measurements.sample_notes: WAL is uncheckpointed in this test (no checkpoint ran). Root revision advances by 4 to 8 per owner commit; its cause was not analysed. Owner freelist stayed at 0. The run-a and run-b sample lines are identical.
measurements.not_measured: Three-transcript shape. Reaching it needs clean restarts (ReserveCleanRestart with retired observations), which this test does not drive. A Store or provider fixture from cmd/tbound was not run.

headroom_red.assertion: No page ceiling may admit ReserveEffect and then refuse its terminal outcome. Authority must not be consumed unless terminal headroom is proven.

boundaries_from_run_b.reserve: refused before receipt (SQLITE_FULL 13 at event append)

headroom_red.summary: first_terminal_admitted_slack=40; reserve_without_terminal_slacks=23. Reserve growth is 17 pages (39 to 56), and terminal growth is 23 pages (56 to 79), both for the one-transcript shape.
headroom_red.consequence: A reservation admitted in this window consumes authority and returns a receipt. Its terminal outcome cannot be written to the owner. The effect is then unresolved and must stay blocked, but the required terminal record is not durable.

physical_reserve_plan.wal_bound_evidence: owner wal_autocheckpoint=1000 pages (sqlite_linux.go:257, 351), about 4.12 MB of WAL at 4120 bytes per frame before an auto-checkpoint attempt. journal_size_limit is not set anywhere in the owner or root code. It only truncates after a successful reset and cannot bound retention by a long reader.
patch_steps: P1 (report only, cmd/tbound/governed_session_linux.go:584): before ReserveEffect, preallocate the derived reserve on the dedicated protected volume (posix_fallocate), then fsync the file and its directory. On failure, return before the receipt. The existing error branch at lines 586-587 already refuses before the callback.

P2 (report only, cmd/tbound/governed_workflow_live_linux.go:751): after RecordTerminalEffectOutcome succeeds, release and fsync the reserve, then continue to provider progress. The volume must stay exclusive from release until terminal completion.

P3 (internal/workflowrecovery/recovery.go:754, ReserveEffect): before commit, require owner headroom at least equal to the terminal bound, so it refuses before the receipt. The bound is not derived yet. It must cover the terminal state, event checkpoint, and proof for the registered transcript count (MaxCleanRestarts+1). The measured one-transcript terminal growth is 23 pages.

P4 (report only, sqlite_linux.go, parent-owned): before the reserve window, run PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) and require busy=0, so the window WAL is only that transaction's frames. journal_size_limit may be added to bound WAL reset size only. It does not bound reader retention.

P5 (deployment): a dedicated protected volume or project quota for owner, root, and audit files, with identity and free-space verified at startup. Stage copies (up to 1 GiB per workspace tree, generations retained with no GC) and the private Git store must sit on a different volume or quota. A stateless statfs check does not reserve capacity.
physical_reserve_plan.patch_step_correction: Superseded 2026-10-15 by Decision 3 of docs/design/d14-reserved-capacity.md (the parent-decision record is not in this repository) (Required terminal-settlement evidence). P2 as written is wrong: the reserve must be released and synced BEFORE the protected terminal writes that need its space, not after terminal durability. This is design ordering only, not implemented. P2 above keeps its original wording. P3's 'the bound is not derived yet' is superseded: the logical owner bound is derived in docs/evidence/d14-headroom-proof-20261015-r3.json. No physical reserve is implemented.
physical_reserve_plan.not_in_patch: No global ProtectedTrustedRoot ticket, no schema change, no generic capacity profile, no all-system writer mutex.

This round did not adopt either.
Choose whether the reserve is held through terminal writes (release after terminal durability) or released before them as in the ext4 experiment. Either requires an exclusive volume.
